questions.B: vertical (perfectly inelastic)
questions.D: upward-sloping
questions.explanation: The firm can sell any quantity at the market price but nothing above it.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In the long run, firms in perfect competition earn only normal profit because
questions.A: free entry of new firms competes away supernormal profit
questions.B: the government taxes all profits above normal
questions.C: consumers refuse to pay high prices
questions.D: the products of different firms are differentiated
questions.explanation: Supernormal profit attracts entrants, raising supply and lowering price until only normal profit remains.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Patents, huge capital requirements and control of raw materials are
questions.A: barriers to entry that help to create monopoly
questions.B: features of perfect competition
questions.D: causes of diseconomies of scale
questions.explanation: Anything that prevents new firms from entering an industry protects the market power of existing firms.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: An electricity company charges industrial users a different tariff per unit from households for the same electricity. This is
questions.B: product differentiation
questions.D: a cartel arrangement
questions.explanation: Charging different prices to different groups for the same product, where the groups can be separated and have different elasticities, is price discrimination.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A monopolist can fix
questions.A: either the price or the quantity sold, but not both
questions.B: both the price and the quantity sold
questions.C: neither the price nor the quantity sold
questions.D: the prices of substitutes as well as his own
questions.explanation: The monopolist faces the market demand curve; once he sets a price, buyers decide the quantity, and vice versa.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's mobile network operators compete mainly through bonus data, adverts and promotions rather than by cutting call prices. This behaviour is typical of
questions.B: price competition in a perfect market
questions.C: output restriction by a pure monopoly
questions.D: exploitation of sellers by a monopsony
questions.explanation: Oligopolists avoid price wars, which hurt all of them, and compete through advertising and product features.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A group of producing countries that agree to restrict output in order to keep prices high is
questions.B: a monopsony
questions.D: a public corporation
questions.explanation: OPEC is the best-known example of a cartel: independent producers acting together like a monopoly.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The main feature that distinguishes monopolistic competition from perfect competition is
questions.B: a single seller
questions.D: a homogeneous product
questions.explanation: Under monopolistic competition many sellers offer similar but not identical products, giving each some price control.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In the colonial era the marketing board was the only buyer of cocoa from all Nigerian farmers. The board was
questions.B: a monopolist
questions.D: a price taker
questions.explanation: A monopsony is a market with a single buyer.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Only two firms supply cement to a region. This market structure is
questions.B: a monopoly
questions.D: monopolistic competition
questions.explanation: Duopoly is the special case of oligopoly with exactly two sellers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Piped water supply is usually provided by one firm because it is cheaper for a single supplier to serve the whole town than for several to lay competing pipelines. This is
questions.B: a legal monopoly
questions.D: perfect competition
questions.explanation: Where economies of scale are so large that one firm can serve the market at the lowest cost, a natural monopoly arises.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A feature common to perfect competition and monopolistic competition is
questions.A: a large number of sellers and freedom of entry
questions.B: a homogeneous product sold by all firms
questions.C: a single firm controlling the market price
questions.D: high barriers preventing new firms from entering
questions.explanation: Both structures have many firms and free entry; they differ in whether the product is homogeneous or differentiated.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Governments usually control monopolies by
questions.B: granting them more patents
questions.C: banning consumers from buying their goods
questions.D: forcing them to raise their prices
questions.explanation: Price regulation, anti-trust laws, removal of entry barriers and public ownership are common controls.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In equilibrium, a perfectly competitive firm produces where price equals
questions.B: average fixed cost
questions.D: average variable cost minus marginal cost
questions.explanation: For the price taker P = AR = MR, and profit is maximised where MR = MC, so P = MC.
